summary: This sermon examines the third sign in John's Gospel—Jesus healing a man crippled for 38 years at the Pool of Bethesda. The pastor argues that while Jesus saves the ashamed and the desperate, he also seeks out the hopeless: those so degraded in soul and identity that they cannot even muster faith or answer his question 'Do you want to be healed?'
key_points: The man (called 'Fred') had been crippled 38 years, isolated, and had lost his identity in his disability
Jesus' healing preceded any recognizable faith—he sought the man out rather than waiting for him to come
We must not universalize our own experience with Jesus or require everyone to come to faith the same way
Identity must be rooted in being God's beloved, not in disability, roles, or accomplishments
Praise and lament are spiritual disciplines for those trapped in hopelessness
big_idea: Jesus seeks out and heals even the most hopeless among us—those who have lost their identity in suffering—demonstrating that God's grace reaches people regardless of their ability to demonstrate faith.
title: Like No Other: Healing the Hopeless
